_comment: The words on the images, grouped by who is reading them.
`lead` is set semibold on its own line and `rest` thin, which is the weight contrast the landing
page's hero uses and the only thing that makes these read as ours rather than as generic store
furniture. `note` is optional and appears small and muted underneath.
The two sets exist because the audiences differ, not because the formats do. The store speaks to
strangers and has to say that punctuation is automatic. `insider` goes to people who already
dictate with VibeVoice every day, to whom that is a premise rather than news -- so those captions
name the thing they have been putting up with instead. Neither set names a competitor or claims a
multiple: accuracy.js is explicit that nothing has been benchmarked.
`shot` is a file in marketing/raw/. `crop`, `zoom` and `focusx` are optional per image and
nothing uses them today; see the note at the top of frame.html for why cropping these captures
turned out to cost more than it bought.
